evidence.note: Recognized scale ('This is large. Let me plan') and decomposed into dedicated modules (ids, cards, errors, store, webhooks, auth, utils, server) — a structured breakdown, but organized around code modules, not an ordered milestone hierarchy with done-conditions. Traps (webhooks, idempotency) got their own modules, so they weren't buried in CRUD.
Got a bootable, auth'd skeleton verifiable early (health endpoint, then Bearer+Basic auth) before layering resources — an 8-flavored 'skeleton first' trait.

Each of the three named traps received its own explicit check: idempotency replay incl. error-body replay, PI state-machine unexpected_state, webhook retry-on-5xx/stop-on-4xx/re-sign. Treated as distinct workstreams with dedicated verification.

Late edge-case sweep (list filters, deleted resources, restricted-key reads) was reactive ('let me re-review before marking complete') rather than driven by a pre-declared milestone acceptance list; done-conditions were emergent, not planned up front.

reasoning: The agent exceeded a flat checklist (anchor 5): it verified a bootable auth'd skeleton early and treated the three traps as distinct workstreams, each with its own module and explicit verification check. But it fell short of anchor 8's deliberate risk-aware sequencing — there was no explicit ordered milestone plan with pre-declared per-milestone done-conditions or dependency articulation; the structure was module-first with emergent, test-driven done-conditions. That interpolates to a 6.
